stories.title: Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever at $83 a share, raising $107.3 billion
stories.summary:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its $70-$78 marketed range, raising $107.3 billion and topping SpaceX's $85.7 billion for the biggest IPO ever, per Gizmodo.

- The roadshow range had implied a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion, well above reports that its expected valuation had fallen to about $1 trillion
- The public S-1 shows soaring revenue and enterprise adoption alongside heavy losses (about $8 billion last year, per Engadget)
- The seven co-founders keep a combined 50.1% of the vote on most matters, and each planned to sell about $250M of shares at the range midpoint
- Amazon is set to make far more from the IPO than Anthropic's VC backers, and the SpaceXAI deal is bigger than previously known
- Risk factors warn that Anthropic's own AI could pose an existential risk
- Blackstone expects credit agencies to rate Anthropic high "junk" after listing, per the FT

stories.title: Nvidia's board rules out reinstating Jensen Huang, ousted as CEO amid espionage and affair scandals
stories.summary:
Jensen Huang, Nvidia's cofounder and CEO of 33 years, is out after the company investigated his affair with a woman US intelligence links to a Chinese spy plot, and the board says it won't bring him back.

- The NYT says the woman is a recruit of China's Ministry of State Security and a top executive at a Singapore AI cloud firm accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China. The relationship reportedly helped route $7.5B in Nvidia AI chips to Chinese firms
- Nvidia's board chair said on the first earnings call since Huang's resignation that the company is not considering reinstating him, despite pressure from Trump, Elon Musk, Silicon Valley executives, and some Nvidia employees
- CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Trump has said he "would not mind" Huang's return but still promotes former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a possible successor
- At her first all-hands as interim CEO, Kress promised across-the-board pay raises and more equity to calm employees, WIRED reports
- Huang agreed to testify before Congress, and Democrats have opened a second investigation into Nvidia's China sales and what they call Huang's "scheme" with Trump
- Nvidia stock slid on the scandal, and investors proposed a class action

stories.title: China's most advanced AI models were trained on export-banned Nvidia chips, as Bloomberg maps a smuggling web centered on Alice Huang
stories.summary:
Evidence is mounting that export controls failed to keep Nvidia's top chips out of Chinese AI labs.

- New research reported by TechCrunch finds China's most advanced AI models were trained on export-banned Nvidia chips
- A Bloomberg investigation mapped a network of Chinese AI companies using smuggled Nvidia chips, with Alice Huang at its center

stories.title: Meta's Muse can now place paid calls to US businesses as it passes 10M users amid mounting controversies
stories.summary:
Meta's Muse, a personal AI agent built on its Muse Spark model platform, keeps adding features and users even as privacy, security, content, and labor controversies mount.

- New: Muse can now place outbound calls to US businesses, but only as a paid feature (TechCrunch)
- Recent features include Apple Watch and Wear OS apps, Spaces for collaborating with the agent, avatar video chat for US users, and a planned Tamagotchi-like Muse wearable
- Meta said on its Q3 earnings call that Muse has over 10 million users; Zuckerberg said a quarter of them shop through the agent, spending about $200 per purchase on average
- Meta suspended Muse's conversation sharing after researchers showed shared links exposed sensitive personal and business data
- Other controversies: OnlyFans creators object to Muse's sexual chat, a since-fixed Mac 0-day, and a contractor "human concierge" reportedly making racist remarks on calls
- Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com; Meta admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw
